title: REALITY FRACTURE DRAFT IS AWESOME!!!
event: FRA early access event (he thanks Wizards for free preview access at 0:03-0:12 and says 'the early access event' at 21:18; first Reality Fracture draft on Arena; event name not shown on screen; he plans five rounds)
source: frames read from data/videos/raw/CWsZxo1pB6Y (tools/video_draft.py frames plus a 1 fps extract of the pack screens); the pack contents of every pick were read from frames, the taken card confirmed from the deck builder at the end (all 42 picks accounted for: 40-card main plus 15 sideboard, with 13 free basics added); transcript from YouTube auto captions, card names corrected; nothing past 24:30 read

colour_path.quote: I could totally just try to splash this card in a black deck
remember, we don't have to be a green deck. We can just be like a black deck

colour_path.main: B base; U or G second
colour_path.quote: I want to lean towards being black base because I could be blue black splashing green or I could just be black green.
a lot of our cards work best in blue black.
maybe we do move back towards just green black if we're going to see cards that late.
my deck is just looking like a fairly standard blue black deck at this point without needing to splash too much stuff.
I'm hoping to be able to just splash green and then maybe splash white as well for this generous revival.
I'm not going to play the amphisana because I'm playing definitely blue black, but I have the tools to splash either white ... or green
I think splashing white is going to be a little bit worse.
splashing green over white is just kind of a no-brainer
I think this deck's going to be pretty good ... Maybe I decide not to splash because I do have plenty of playables, but I think Hapatra is going to be really really strong.

picks.reasoning: Hapatra is a two-for-one (3/3 plus a kill if the graveyard has something in it) and splashable; enough better than No Admittance to take. Synergy with basic landcyclers: cycle Apex Witchstalker, the big card in the graveyard powers Hapatra, and you get the Forest, so any black deck can splash it.

considered.Variable Chaser: the rare; good mostly as a three-mana 2/3 flier with prowess; Ark of Fortune (each player discards their hand and draws seven) is risky
considered.No Admittance: mono-coloured single red pip; would be his second pick, 'a little bit better than the three mana 2/3'

picks.plan: Open. Black-green gold card first, but framed as a splash in any black deck (via landcyclers).
quotes: I think here I'm going to take the Hapatra. I think it's enough better than No Admittance that it's worth taking.
I could totally just try to splash this card in a black deck and it actually really does synergize well with the basic land cycling

picks.reasoning: Wants to try a black graveyard deck around Hapatra; Rewrite Regrets returns a creature or planeswalker (mana value 6 or less) for four mana and empowers Jace. Enters trigger, so it also works with Hapatra.

considered.Compel Brutality: green removal; passed 'but we will try this out for now'

picks.plan: Black graveyard deck; 'we don't have to be a green deck, we can just be a black deck that tries to get this to work'.
quotes: I think I'm going to try this rewrite regrets thing and see if I can make a black potential graveyard deck work.
remember, we don't have to be a green deck. We can just be like a black deck

picks.reasoning: Likes the uncommon: every surveil lets him pay to put a +1/+1 counter on Proft and draw, and Empower Jace cards can tick down by one to get Proft going. Between Proft and Arcane Amphisbaena (also nice with Hapatra); still taking power level over the blue-black land.

considered.Arcane Amphisbaena: 'mostly between the Proft and the Amphisbaena'; works with Hapatra, empowers Jace
considered.Way of the Warlord: 'pretty nice', gives the Jace extra abilities
considered.Theorix Annex: blue-black land, not taking it 'I'm still taking power level cards'

picks.plan: Black base, green or blue second.
quotes: I'm still taking power level cards. Um, I think it's mostly between the Prof and the Amphisbaena.

picks.reasoning: Mabel, Bitter Recluse as a defensive body for a defensive black-green-blue deck (removes counters from a creature or planeswalker, so it answers a Jace token or a +1/+1 counter). Mabel, Valley Hero (RW) is reasonable but 'so far from what I'm doing'.

considered.Mabel, Valley Hero: reasonable RW one-drop, not taking it

picks.plan: 'I want to lean towards being black base because I could be blue black splashing green or I could just be black green.' Sees red and white cards flowing; blue-black looks open.
quotes: I think I want to lean towards being black base because I could be blue black splashing green or I could just be black green.
Okay, it's looking like blue black is open which is nice.

picks.reasoning: Takes the rare to get experience with it; it mills three on entering and grows by +2/+2 for every seven cards in the graveyard, so good in a self-mill deck. Sticks to black cards.

considered.Paradox Shaper: one-three that mills three and re-prepares itself; 'could be good', would like one copy later

picks.plan: Black, self-mill; red is also flowing but he sticks to black.
quotes: I'm going to try taking the rare. We'll get some experience with the rare.
I'm going to just stick to my black cards for now.

picks.reasoning: Curve check (two one-drops already). Void Extrapolator is a two-two that mills three, so it is close to a one-mana 3/2 early and sets up Hapatra and the graveyard cards. Expects to get Keeper of the Quiet Hour later.

considered.Clash of Elements: 'very strong' but he does not want to splash in that direction
considered.Keeper of the Quiet Hour: hopes to get it a bit later

picks.plan: Black-blue graveyard; not splashing red.
quotes: Let's try taking the void extrapolator. It kind of plays into this graveyard theme

picks.reasoning: Explains Echoverse pairs (the mirror-verse version and the main-universe version; often three of them in a pack). Takes the card-filtering Arni over Silence the Echo because he only wants one effect of that type.

considered.Silence the Echo: pretty efficient removal but 'I only really want one of this type of effect'
considered.Arni, Renowned Champion: the other half of the pair, not wanted

picks.plan: 'We are pretty sure we're playing black, but I think a lot of our cards work best in blue black.'
quotes: I'd rather just get the Arie Humble Scribe as a nice card filtering addition to my deck.

picks.reasoning: Few blue cards in the pool so far; takes the white-black land to keep a white splash open ('maybe I would want to splash white for something') over Inspired Tethermage.
picks.plan: Still black with blue; could be RB or GB 'technically', but most cards work best in blue-black.
quotes: I might take the meticulous commons though because maybe I would want to splash white for something.
I'm just going to take the land here over the tether mage, I think.

picks.reasoning: A flier with basic landcycling: works with Hapatra and keeps a white splash open. Self-mill pieces and Murmuring Volume (fixing) also in the pack.

considered.Something Worth Saving: mill four, a permanent into the hand; 'good for selection, finding something like a Hapatra'

picks.plan: Black-blue, Hapatra splash.
quotes: I think that undulating Witness is nice. It's a flyer. It has basic land cycling to work with my Hepatra or if I wanted to splash white or something like that.

picks.reasoning: Cannot cast it until the graveyard is deep, but can discard it for early interaction; a scary card with a full graveyard.

considered.Theorix Metamage: would work fine with the graveyard theme

picks.plan: Black-blue graveyard.
quotes: I think Prof is going to be a pretty scary card if I can get my graveyard full, and I'm going to be trying to do that.

picks.reasoning: Green cards are coming back late ('we have gotten back some of these green cards'), which makes him think green could be open; Amphisbaena is a good combo with Hapatra and empowers Jace. Might move back towards green-black.

considered.Murmuring Volume: three-mana rock; the pick tag sat on it before the pick

picks.plan: 'maybe we do move back towards just green black if we're going to see cards that late.'
quotes: We have gotten back some of these green cards, so that does make me think that maybe that deck will be open.
Let's just take the ais bane and maybe we do move back towards just green black

picks.reasoning: Returns a mana value 3 creature from the graveyard with an initial counter; 'honestly could be okay'. Keeps a white splash possible. The pick tag sat on Konstrari Annex while he decided; Generous Revival is confirmed by the sideboard.

considered.Konstrari Annex: pick tag on it at one point, not taken

picks.plan: Blue-black 'fairly standard' deck 'without needing to splash too much'.
quotes: I already have the potential to splash white a little bit and we get the theorix metamage kind of last. Blue black is looking fairly open.

picks.reasoning: Comes last in the pack, which he reads as blue-black being fairly open; does not mind having passed the three-mana mana rock.
picks.plan: Blue-black, mostly standard, little splashing.
quotes: I don't mind passing up on the like three mana mana rock for my cards here because mostly my deck is just looking like a fairly standard blue black deck at this point without needing to splash too much stuff.

picks.reasoning: Last card, auto-selected; no comment.

Wants one Paradox Shaper as a late-game card to assemble (fills the graveyard on turbo mode; mill the whole deck and stack it); also improves Dark Matter Manipulator and Proft. It is slow, but his deck has early defences already. Hapatra, the Desert Frost (stun counter, four-mana tempo play) is 'more important' in a four-drop slot that is empty, but he takes the Shaper.

considered.Hapatra, the Desert Frost: tempo play at four mana, four-drop slot 'a little bit empty'; 'I think this card might be more important though' (about the Shaper)
considered.Icy Reception: cheap counter spell that becomes a combat trick
considered.Silence the Echo: 'I do need some removal at some point', but focuses on Paradox Shaper

picks.plan: Blue-black, self-mill.
quotes: I really want to have one in this deck, I think, as kind of a nice cool late game card to maybe assemble.
I do need some removal at some point, but I think right now I'm just going to focus on getting my Paradox Shaper.

picks.reasoning: Takes the land: 'nothing crazy for me here'. The pack still holds all three Echoverse cards, so no information on which colours are open. Another white land is there too; thinks he could splash Hapatra and Generous Revival and hopes to wheel a land or Murmuring Volume.

considered.Meticulous Commons: another white land; hopes it wheels
considered.Arcane Amphisbaena: another copy, 'I'm just going to try to stick to my blue black deck'

picks.plan: Blue-black base; splash Hapatra (green) and Generous Revival (white).
quotes: I think I'm just going to take the land here. There's nothing crazy for me here.
Honestly, I could try to splash the Hatra and maybe splash the generous revival if I'm milling enough.

picks.reasoning: Lacked interaction. Multiply by Zero (target creature has base power and toughness 0 until end of turn) kills nearly every creature in his deck's matchup space because none of his cards has +1/+1 counters; cannot kill a card that gets a counter or threshold boost. 'Getting a removal spell is nice.'

considered.Surgical Precision: white removal, would be the splash if he needed white instead of green

picks.plan: Blue-black; green splash for Hapatra, maybe white for Generous Revival.
quotes: I was mentioning I was kind of lacking interaction.
I'm hoping to be able to just splash green and then maybe splash white as well for this generous revival.

picks.reasoning: 'There's not really a card that I want here.' Could splash Compel Brutality but takes the Jace: kind of expensive, but plus one draws a card most of the time and in a stable position it takes over the game and threatens to win.
picks.plan: Blue-black planeswalker/graveyard.
quotes: there's not really a card that I want here I mean I could try to splash compel brutality, but I might as well try this Jace out. I think he looks reasonable. He is kind of expensive, but he's like plus one to draw a card a lot of the time.

picks.reasoning: Takes the green-black land because it makes Hapatra easier to play; the Empower Jace card (Way of the Necromancer) is also on his radar. Terminal Criticism is one of a cycle of sideboard cards. Does not want a 1/2 flier for two (Geist of Saint Thalia). Protege's Awakening 'is fine'.

considered.Way of the Necromancer: 'My grand project unfolds', empowers Jace, loyalty counter when a creature dies; kept in mind
considered.Geist of Saint Thalia: 'I don't really want a one two flyer for two'

picks.plan: Blue-black with green splash for Hapatra.
quotes: I'm just going to take the green black land. It makes it a little bit easier to play this Hatra. And I am hoping to play the Hapatra because I think it's going to be pretty good in my deck.

picks.reasoning: 'I have a lot of self mill': Blessed Ghoul comes back from the graveyard, so he wants the first copy; saw one earlier (P1p4). Twinned Vision is fine too, as a card to mill over for value.

considered.Tetsuko Umezawa, Fugitive: 'a two mana one three blocker is not huge' but works with a lot of his cards (makes power-one creatures unblockable); 'it's okay'
considered.Twinned Vision: 'fine' as a card to mill over for value

picks.plan: Self-mill graveyard value deck.
quotes: I think I might just take the blessed ghoul though. I have a lot of self mill.

picks.reasoning: 'Such a great pickup for my deck': hand disruption, exiles a nonland card he can later cast with threshold using mana of any type. 'This card is going to be the best card in my deck', seventh pick of pack two.

picks.plan: Blue-black, graveyard/threshold.
quotes: Ooh, baby. Null Summoner is such a great pickup for my deck.
this card is going to be the best card in my deck. And I got it seventh pick in pack two.

picks.reasoning: Already has a couple of dual lands to help splash white or green, and might splash only one of the two. Necromancer is a bonus resource if milled (returns another creature from the graveyard to hand).
picks.plan: Blue-black base; splash white (Generous Revival) or green (Hapatra); only one of them.
quotes: I'm going to just take theoretical necromancer. I already have a couple of dual lands to maybe help splash white, maybe help splash green. I might just only try to splash one of the colors

Confirmed by the deck screen (Bestial Incursion in the pool, Icy Reception not).

considered.Icy Reception: 'a nice cheap counter spell', passed in the end; the pick tag stayed on it
considered.Greenhouse Propagator: 'the two mana play would be fine'

picks.plan: Blue-black; green splash gets a second card (Bestial Incursion next to Hapatra); white splash (Generous Revival) now less likely.
quotes: I changed my mind. I think the two mana play would be fine, but I already have a couple of two drops. I already have a couple one drops. My deck doesn't really hold its mana up particularly well because I'm mostly playing at sorcery speed
getting a another really good green card to help me with my self mill seems pretty reasonable.

picks.reasoning: 'I'm going to take murmuring volume now. We'll see if we want that.' Fixing for the splash; Meticulous Commons (white-black land) left in the pack.

considered.Meticulous Commons: left in the pack (second one in the same pack as Murmuring Volume, which wheeled from P2p2)

picks.plan: Blue-black with green splash.

picks.reasoning: No separate comment for this pick; his next words are about the green splash ('splashing white is going to be a little bit worse'). Confirmed by the deck screen (two Way of the Necromancer in the pool, no Blazing Crescendo).
picks.plan: Splash green rather than white: Bestial Incursion is 'a very similar vibe' to Generous Revival, a card to mill over for value.

picks.reasoning: Last card, auto-selected.

considered.Way of the Mind Sculptor: 'good card draw' (empower Jace 5, draw a card when removing two or more loyalty)

quotes: I think I need I have plenty of card draw. I've got good value. I just want more kill spells and I think that's a little bit better than last gasp. Though it's close.
Mindseeker Oculus is also great. So I love that card.

picks.reasoning: On-colour blue-black card with three modes (counter a creature spell unless its controller pays two, -2/-2, or mill three then draw). Liking the green splash; does not love Way of the Necromancer ('we could consider it').
picks.plan: Blue-black with green splash.
quotes: I'm honestly liking my uh I think my um green splash is looking pretty reasonable.
just taking the blue black on color card is going to be great

considered.Tinybones, Pocket Nuisance: 'pretty nice' as a discard three-drop with a reasonable body

picks.reasoning: 'Oh my gosh, Null Summoner number two.' Also happy about the two Theorix Charms, which makes passing the blue counter spell (Icy Reception) for Bestial Incursion feel less bad.
